body.statement: Can the rational finite-support family \(\{\mathbf P_\theta:\theta\in\Theta_0\cup\Theta_1\}\) in Definition \(\mathrm{def:simultaneous-perturbation-family}\) be chosen so that \(\operatorname{TV}_{\mathrm{mix}}\le1/4\), \(\Delta_{N,K}>0\) has explicit \(K\), \(d\), and logarithmic order, and every alternative rematching column has certified nonnegative reduced cost \(\mathfrak g_{\mathrm{rem}}\ge0\), with strict slack away from the declared contact columns? If no such additive-complexity family exists, does \(\mathcal F_{K,d}^{\mathrm{joint}}\) instead admit a two-sided localized covering or Rademacher bound controlled by \(r=\min\{K,d\}\)?
body.justification: This dichotomy is the genuine proof boundary behind the remaining small-\(K\) minimax gap.
body.gap: Hundrieser--Staudt--Munk transfer entropy between two \(c\)-conjugate potentials, while no located result controls a simultaneous \(K\)-tuple for the repulsive squared-sum cost.
body.consumer: Resolving the aggregate dual complexity determines whether the empirical MOT estimator is rate-optimal or must be replaced.

obligation.what_is_open: Construct, uniformly in \(K\), a simultaneous-marginal finite family with explicit endpoint separation, mixture total variation at most \(1/4\), and nonnegative reduced cost for every rematching column, or replace the sum of the \(K\) marginal concave-process bounds by a two-sided shared-geometric complexity theorem controlled by \(r=\min\{K,d\}\).
obligation.obstruction: The dimension-controlled support diameter restricts optimal sums but does not bound the total sensitivity of all \(K\) dual potentials. Tensoring two-margin hard instances requires orthogonal directions and saturates after at most \(d\) blocks; no supplied finite family has a reduced-cost certificate that survives all cross-arm rematchings.
obligation.attempted: The subset exchange and common-support interpolation routes were completed. The parity, orthogonal, Bernoulli-knot, and two-margin constructions certify boundary cases, but none accumulates a growing-\(K\) separation. The supplied finite-LP checks for \(K=3,\ldots,8\) do not specify a parameterized hard family and therefore cannot certify the required all-column lower construction.
obligation.partial_result:
The proved common-support interpolation inequality is
\[
\left|\frac{V(\mathbf Q)-V(\mathbf P)}{K^2}\right|
\le \frac1{K^2}\left|\sum_k\int\|x\|_2^2\,d(Q_k-P_k)\right|
+\sum_k\sup_{g\in\mathcal C_{2(2\sqrt d+1)/K^2}}
\left|\int g\,d(Q_k-P_k)\right|,
\]
and it yields the uniform upper bound \(C_d\{N^{-1/2}+\min(r/K^2,K^{-1}m^{-2/d})\}\). The support exchange theorem also proves diameter \(2\sqrt r\). These are computable upper-side certificates, but they neither construct a simultaneous indistinguishable family nor reduce the sum of the \(K\) marginal empirical complexities.
